transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maria Lopez (Pelagia CTO), Ben Wallace (Pelagia ML Eng), Priya Nair (Pelagia Head of Infra), Samir Qureshi (Pelagia Security)

Summary: quick discovery focused on model selection — open models, context length, multilingual support, and tool-calling/function-calling compatibility. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for latency and data residency.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, AE on the account, with Samira our SE. Quick intros — Maria, Ben, Priya, do you want to say hi?
[00:07] Maria Lopez: Hi, Maria here, CTO. We're looking at using LLMs inside our analytics product, must be private data friendly.
[00:12] Ben Wallace: Ben, ML eng — primarily model selection and inference cost are top of mind.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Priya — infra. We need to understand networking and VPC options and if we need full on-prem.
[00:19] Samira Patel: Great, thanks. Maybe start high level: what are your workloads and requirements?
[00:23] Ben Wallace: Mainly document Q&A across 30 languages, lots of legal / regulatory text which can be long. We see context lengths up to 100k tokens in some docs but typical is 8k-32k. Latency target is sub-800ms for short queries, but for long context retrieval paths we can accept higher. Cost is a big constraint — we have to keep inference spend predictable.
[00:40] Alex Chen: OK so two axes: context length and multilingual accuracy + cost. Are you leaning toward open models or proprietary APIs?
[00:47] Maria Lopez: We prefer open models for licensing and control, but we need managed infra — we don't want to manage a thousand GPUs. Hosted is attractive but our compliance team wants VPC options and audit logs.
[00:57] Samira Patel: That aligns with how customers use Redwood — hosted for quick test and production if data residency allows it, dedicated for reserved capacity, and private for VPC/on-prem. For model selection, common open families are Llama-3 variants, Mistral (mix of instruct), Falcon, and some newer 70B+ models; also Mosaic and OpenLlama forks. Any preference for model family?
[01:15] Ben Wallace: We've benchmarked Llama 2->3 and Mistral a bit; Llama3 tokens are higher quality on our prompts, Mistral-instruct is cheaper and good for short chats. But we need function/tool calling support for structured outputs (we call tools to fetch DB results). So model must handle tool-calling or Redwood's function-calling layer needs to map reliably.
[01:34] Samira Patel: Good point — Redwood supports function/tool-calling via structured output and emits events to your tool runner. Some models have better structured-output calibration. We can recommend a few: Llama-3 70B quantized (better instruction following and tool-calling), Mistral-Instruct 7B/14B for cheaper flows, and if you need long context, Redwood supports extended context variants (we've onboarded bespoke 100k-context models for some customers).
[01:55] Priya Nair: About extended context — how does that work operationally? Does that mean we need Dedicated or Private?
[02:01] Samira Patel: Operationally, extended context increases memory load. For hosting, we have hosted endpoints with specialized routing and chunking; for consistent high throughput >50 concurrent long-context sessions, Dedicated or Private with pinned GPU pools is recommended. We also offer prefix/KV caching so repeated docs don't re-run full context.
[02:17] Ben Wallace: KV cache — is that per-customer and encrypted?
[02:21] Samira Patel: Yes, KV cache is tenant-isolated and can be encrypted at rest with customer KMS in Private. In Hosted we manage keys but we do offer Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) for enterprise.
[02:31] Samir Qureshi: SOC2, audit logs — we need those, and SAML SSO. Also, can you confirm retention policies and where logs live?
[02:37] Alex Chen: We are SOC2 compliant, we have audit logs and SSO integrations. For Hosted enterprise customers we can configure log forwarding and retention; Private gives you the most control over where logs and artifacts live. Samira will share the security pack after.
[02:46] Maria Lopez: On model quality, multilingual: We need strong performance across Spanish, French, German, Mandarin, Portuguese, and occasional Arabic. How do open models compare?
[02:56] Samira Patel: In general Llama-3 shows decent multilingual; Mistral tends to be stronger in European languages, and for Chinese we usually recommend specialized Chinese-trained variants or instruction-tuned Llama3-s with evals. Redwood's model catalog has verified perf profiles per language — we can run a quick eval with your sample text.
[03:15] Ben Wallace: Great. About function/tool calling — can we do tool calling with Dedicated if model is quantized? We plan to use INT8/4 quantized models to save cost.
[03:23] Samira Patel: Quantization can affect output calibration; for most tool-calling we support quantized kernels that preserve function calling behavior. There's a small hit sometimes on structured JSON outputs — for critical pipelines we recommend mixed: use quantized for most traffic and a non-quantized model variant for tool-and-critical flows (we can route automatically).
[03:39] Alex Chen: Also worth mentioning smart routing — you can route by policy (latency vs cost), and Redwood can do fallback to a higher-capacity or non-quantized model for a specific route.
[03:47] Ben Wallace: Nice. For benchmarks — what does Redwood need from us?
[03:50] Samira Patel: Ideally: representative prompts, sample documents (anonymized), target latency threshold, and a scope: e.g., 5k queries/day with 30k token contexts for the 10% tail. We'll run hosted and dedicated variants and share token-level cost/latency breakdown.
[04:04] Priya Nair: Networking — if we go VPC, what are the egress requirements? How does private control plane get set up?
[04:10] Samira Patel: For VPC we integrate via private peering and customer-managed NATs. Private control plane communicates over the peered control channel; you can also choose on-prem package for air-gapped. We'll send the network diagram in the security pack.
[04:22] Maria Lopez: Any notes on data residency EU? We're partly in EU, partly US.
[04:26] Alex Chen: You can pin regions for routing and we have EU-hosted clusters. Private deployment is often chosen when strict residency is required.
[04:32] Ben Wallace: Can we do a hybrid — some traffic hosted, some private? For now we'd like to pilot hosted for experimentation and Dedicated for production.
[04:39] Samira Patel: Absolutely — many customers start hosted for evaluation, then move critical, high-volume routes to Dedicated, with Private as the compliance option. We can configure canary rollouts.
[04:49] Ben Wallace: On the open-model choices — which exact checkpoints do you recommend we start with for our use case?
[04:54] Samira Patel: For multilingual + tool-calling + long context I'd suggest: Llama-3 70B (instruction-tuned) as primary for quality; a Mistral-Instruct 14B for cheaper/default paths; try a 70B extended-context variant for any 50k-100k workflows; and keep a small 7-8B inflight model (Mistral or Falcon-7B) for light queries to save cost. We'll provide pre-run eval matrices.
[05:15] Maria Lopez: For pricing and commitment, what does Dedicated look like? We have sporadic spikes — autoscaling needs to be clear.
[05:22] Alex Chen: Dedicated can do reserved capacity + burst to shared capacity; commitments reduce unit cost. We'll outline example configs in the worksheet. For spikes we recommend a mix of dedicated baseline with burst to hosted or a fallback routing policy.
[05:34] Priya Nair: One more on observability — can we get token-level RBAC and traceability per user?
[05:38] Samira Patel: Yes — Redwood Console supports per-route metrics, token-level breakdowns, traces, and RBAC tied to your SAML. You can tie regressions to prompt sets and triggers.
[05:47] Ben Wallace: Ok that helps. Any potential gotchas with function/tool calling and chain-of-tools?
[05:52] Samira Patel: Two things to watch: JSON-schema calibration (we provide output validators and function-calling wrappers), and latency compounding across tool chains — we recommend async tool workers and caching for idempotent calls. We'll help you instrument traces.
[06:07] Alex Chen: To summarize next steps: Alex will send pricing + capacity worksheet, Samira will share security pack and network diagram, Ben will provide sample prompts and dataset for evaluation, Priya will confirm compliance constraints. We'll schedule a tech deep dive and a benchmark run the week of Oct 26.
[06:22] Maria Lopez: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[06:24] Priya Nair: No from infra, thank you.
[06:25] Ben Wallace: Thanks. We'll try to get the dataset over by Monday.
[06:29] Alex Chen: Great, we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript. Notes: occasional transcription artifacts and mis-heard model names in auto transcript (e.g., 'Llama three' sometimes recorded as 'lama three'); speaker labels may shift in places.
